messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD ALERT — GPU queue length > 10k on cluster 'east-1-prod'. Autoscaler attempted scale but hit max_nodes for pool 'gpu-large'. Throttling 503s observed. Paging infra-oncall.
alex: seeing it, joining. quick snapshot: queue backlog across the inference queue, tokens/sec dropped ~40%.
maya: on it. can you paste autoscaler logs?
alex: logs show repeated FailedEviction / insufficient resources for pods: 'no compatible node with requested MIG slices' and 'binpacking conflict'. snippet:```text
E0521 03:12:10 scheduler.go:345] binding failed: 0/120 nodes are available: 90 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 30 NodeLabelMismatch.
autoscaler: scaleUp: attempted 12 nodes; request denied (max_nodes reached).
```
sam: looks like MIG fragmentation — many nodes have leftover 1/4 slices but requests need 1/2 or full. capacity is technically there but unusable.
rachel: customers seeing 503s? CS reports two enterprise tenants with timeouts on embeddings and chat. severity looking like P1.
ops-lead: escalate to P1; put status page in maintenance (brief msg). rachel, draft customer-safe wording: short note + ETA for mitigation.
rachel: drafting: "We're investigating intermittent 503s for inference endpoints. Mitigating now; will update in 30m." ok?
ops-lead: yes. post it.
alex: immediate mitigations I can try in parallel: 1) force evict low-priority batch pods to free contiguous MIG slices 2) trigger manual node add (temporarily bump pool limit) 3) run drain/recreate on worst-fragmented nodes to defragment binpack.
maya: I can take 1 and 3. sam, can you coordinate manual scaling with cloud perms?
sam: I can bump node pool to +6 if this is approved. note: we've been conservative due to quota. ops-lead, approve?
ops-lead: approve temporary +6. keep us posted. :thumbsup:
alex: starting evictions on batch-ml jobs (low-priority q). command:```bash
kubectl delete pod -l job=batch-ml -n ml-prod --grace-period=10
```
(doing gentle kills to reduce risk).
maya: I'm running a targeted drain on node gnode-23 and gnode-47 (they have many 1/4-MIG fragments). command:```bash
kubectl cordon gnode-23 && kubectl drain gnode-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n gpu-pool
```
these will reschedule into other nodes hopefully creating larger contiguous free slices.
sam: manual nodepool increase started. creating 6 nodes now. cloud console shows provisioning.
deploy-bot: canary deploys paused for inference queues.
alex: checking scheduler traces: here's a candidate error from kube-scheduler:```text
fit predicate failed: nodeAffinity mismatch; preferredDuringScheduling ignored; leftover slice mismatch (MIG-size).
```
so even after adding nodes, if new nodes are different MIG configurations we could still fragment. need to align MIG sizes for newly provisioned nodes.
maya: good catch. creating new nodes with same MIG profile as majority: profile 1g. started an instance template with MIG=1g.
sam: new nodes are up. verifying with `nvidia-smi mig -cgi` shows uniform 1g slices.
alex: after drains + new nodes, scheduler placed ~120 pending pods in the last 5m. queue length down from 10k -> 2.3k. tokens/sec improving.
ops-lead: nice. what about stranded capacity messages? any nodes with idle GPU slices that are incompatible?
maya: one odd node gnode-99 has 2x 1/4 slices free but no pod fits them (pods request 1/2). I'll mark for later full resize.
sam: temp policy: allow fractional packing for non-critical routes (reduce request size via serving config) — can push a small config change to allow 1/4 allocations for reranker jobs. alex, can you add a fallback to smaller model to reduce GPU footprint?
alex: yes, we can route low-priority rerank to quantized 8-bit model and fallback to CPU if necessary. pushing routing change now.
deploy-bot: routing change rolled to 25% -> 100% in 4m.
rachel: customer-impact update: enterprise-A: intermittent 503s resolved for embeddings, enterprise-B still degraded for chat. posting update to status page now.
ops-lead: offload notes for SRE postmortem: root cause preliminary: MIG sizing mix in autoscaled pool + tight max_nodes cap -> autoscaler refused to add nodes -> backlog growth -> scheduler binpacking constraints -> stranded fractional GPU capacity. add follow-ups: increase autoscaler headroom, homogenize MIG profile, enable emergency rebalance job.
maya: handing off to alex for next steps; I need a quick break. alex, you on-call for the next hour?
alex: taking on-call. I'll keep iterating on drain/recreate + more targeted resizes. maya, tx.
maya: leaving a short runbook snippet in thread:```text
Mitigation steps (quick):
1) Evict low-priority jobs
2) Add nodes with matching MIG profile (avoid mix)
3) Drain badly fragmented nodes to allow binpack consolidation
4) If pinned, rescale MIG on salvage nodes and restart kubelet
5) Push routing fallbacks for non-critical customers
```
alex: implementing 2 & 3 now. starting nodepool resume + template swap.
sam: FYI autoscaler team, we'll follow up to increase max_nodes by default for this pool and add a check that rejects heterogeneous MIG templates. filing ticket INFRA-7421.
ops-lead: make sure we capture customer list and expected RCA timeline. rachel will coordinate comms.
rachel: posted second update: "Mitigation in progress; partial recovery observed; next update in 30m."
alex: monitoring: queue now ~900, token/sec 85% of baseline. starting to uncordon safe nodes.
maya: rebalancer script finished moving 40 pods off gnode-47. fragmentation reduced.
ops-lead: good work. set severity to P1 -> P2 when we hit steady-state recovery.
alex: confirmed — recovery trend, but we'll keep pool at +4 temporary for 3 hours.
rachel: prepping customer postmortem note template.
ops-lead: handoff complete. alex remains on-call. if any regression, page the infra-oncall channel. great coordination everyone :clap:
